prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (keep safety authority). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; records AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate per cancellation baseline); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; Passenger Misconnect Count weighting if approved). DPS/CAM/SAE/DMS reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse (PAW; role-limited; delay absorption DPS vs SAE vs realized times; queue/slot adherence; applies fuel/emissions factors by aircraft category, phase, delay location); Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Common Situation Display (current/aging/stale/unavailable); Contingency Operations Console; Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report (benefits vs trade-offs: delay, queue, slot, cancellation, emissions). Silverpine accepts emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time) and Aircraft Operator Representative (challenge cancellation avoidance via Decision Log); Regional Flow Manager (advanced training); Slot Coordinator; Data Governance Steward (disputed values; published measures cite sources, versions, confidence, exclusions); Meteorology Briefing Officer (flags weather-dominated fuel periods); Airport Duty Manager (receives benefit summaries: stand occupancy, surface congestion, recovery, passenger disruption); Tower Supervisor (trained on TSM, DMS, Arrival Regulation Console, runway meters); Air traffic controllers; System Support Engineer. Metrics: cancellation avoidance vs baseline; emissions separate real reductions from delay transfers; benefits allocated to operators, airports, ANS, handling, passengers. Role-based training: normal, constrained, recovery, degraded. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction; Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance (adherence priority); Contingency Fallback (ADM declares after consulting RFM).

New part:
S867: Ramp personnel shall be trained under the direction of the Ramp Control Lead to use the Ramp Movement Board without substituting system indications for required visual checks, radio coordination, and local safety procedures.
S868: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative shall be trained to submit, review, and update Flight Intent Message data through approved interfaces and to assess the operational effect of Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time changes.
S869: Ground handling personnel shall be trained by the Ground Handling Dispatcher on the Handling Resource Planner and on procedures for confirming that resource constraints are represented accurately before they influence collaborative decisions.
S870: The Slot Coordinator shall receive training on the Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, and applicable Business Rules Registry entries so that slot actions are applied consistently and transparently.
S871: The Network Operations Liaison and Airspace Sector Planner shall be trained to coordinate regional constraints, sector load conditions, and network measures using the Sector Load Monitor and Common Situation Display.
S872: The Airport Duty Manager shall be trained to recognize when an Airport Capacity Plan requires revision and when the operational state should move from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State.
S873: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall be trained to explain weather uncertainty in operational terms and to verify that the Weather Ingest Gateway supports the assumptions used during briefings.
S874: The Emergency Response Coordinator shall participate in recurrent training so that emergency priorities are integrated into flow management decisions without obscuring command authority or safety responsibilities.
S875: The Deicing Coordinator shall receive seasonal refresher training on how deicing capacity assumptions are represented in demand and departure metering tools.
S876: The Data Governance Steward shall train operational users on data quality responsibilities, privacy expectations, and the correct interpretation of audit records in the Audit Event Ledger.
S877: The System Support Engineer shall train superusers on service status checks, access fault escalation, and safe use of the Contingency Operations Console during partial outages.
S878: Initial training shall include classroom instruction, supervised workstation practice, scenario walkthroughs in the Digital Briefing Room, and observed operational shadowing before independent system use is authorized.
S879: Recurrent training shall be required at least annually and after major changes to the Regional Flow Platform, Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, or Flight Data Exchange.
S880: Simulation exercises shall use realistic traffic samples, weather constraints, surface congestion, airline schedule pressure, handling resource shortages, and recovery objectives to test coordinated decision making.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
